findings: Sutton–Barto Chs. 5–6 supply episodic Monte Carlo, TD(0), Sarsa, and Q-learning algorithms and the relevant exploration/importance-sampling conventions. Monte Carlo return methods are stated for episodic tasks whose episodes terminate under every selected action.

A Q-learning convergence claim needs a stationary finite discounted model, bounded rewards, infinite visitation of every state-action pair, per-pair Robbins–Monro step sizes, and the theorem’s bounded martingale-noise condition. The textbook cites external convergence proofs and does not provide the complete stochastic-approximation argument.

The book expressly leaves the exploring-starts Monte Carlo control convergence proof open; algorithm presentation must not be represented as that theorem. Ordinary importance sampling can have infinite variance; weighted estimates have different finite-sample bias.

findings: The source defines sample complexity on a realized infinite path as the number of times V^{pi_t}(s_t)<V*(s_t)-epsilon; its high-probability polynomial bound allows bad steps to occur at any times and is not an output-only permanent-stopping guarantee.

R-MAX and Delayed Q-learning have separate admissible-heuristic theorems and sample thresholds. Suppressing logarithms with the uninformative Vmax=(1-gamma)^-1 yields leading orders S^2 A/[epsilon^3(1-gamma)^6] and S A/[epsilon^4(1-gamma)^8], respectively; these do not replace the more refined heuristic-dependent bounds.

The source explicitly flags adaptive online transition concentration as needing a martingale argument whose details it refers elsewhere. Conditional Hoeffding/Azuma suppliers are usable only after that sampling/filtration match is established.

findings: The complete JMLR article gives the finite communicating MDP/diameter assumptions, UCRL2 confidence sets and extended-value-iteration algorithm, and proves its upper bound.

Theorem 2’s exact bound is 34 D S sqrt(A T log(T/delta)) with probability at least 1-delta for every initial state and T>=1. Theorem 5’s expected lower bound 0.015 sqrt(D S A T) applies only when integer S,A>=10, D>=20 log_A S, and T>=D S A.
The theorem is for average reward, not discounted return; finite diameter/communication cannot be dropped or silently extended to transient/uncommunicating models.

findings: Sutton–Barto displays the episodic policy-gradient theorem proof, starting with a fixed start state and undiscounted terminating episodes; the policy gradient is expressed through occupancy/action-value terms.

The REINFORCE trajectory score estimator with return-to-go is unbiased when differentiation can pass through the trajectory law and score/return terms are integrable. An integrable state-only baseline preserves the expected update because conditional expected policy score is zero.
The source gives algorithm identities, not nonlinear/deep actor–critic optimizer convergence. Continuing average-reward results require the separately stated ergodic steady-state distribution.
